documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Routine check. No relapses since mid-2020. Has not needed the MS clinic since the transfer visit last year. Some injection-night achiness, takes it in stride. Bladder: urgency most days but no accidents, oxybutynin before long drives or meetings. Dry mouth when she uses it, tolerable.

O: Vitals as charted. Comfortable. Pupils equal, no APD. Strength full, reflexes symmetric, gait normal.

A/P: RRMS stable on interferon beta-1a. Neurogenic bladder, urgency without incontinence, PRN oxybutynin working. Monitoring labs due in May, order in. Physical in the fall, Pap then.

documents.title: Monitoring labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Normal CBC and hepatic panel. Faxed to MS clinic.

documents.title: Oxybutynin refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax: oxybutynin 5 mg tab, #180, no refills remaining. Last seen 3/2022, physical booked October. Pended for PCP, approved x1 with 1 refill.

reports.text: Specimen: liquid-based cervical cytology with high-risk HPV co-test. Specimen adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Preventive visit, 30F.

Since last year: no new neuro symptoms. Interferon three nights a week. Bladder unchanged, urgency only, no leakage, no UTIs ever. Busy season at work. No new meds.

ROS negative except mild dry mouth with oxybutynin.

Exam: Vitals as charted. NAD. Eyes: no APD, EOM full. Neck: thyroid not enlarged. CV regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap with HPV obtained. Neuro: strength 5/5, reflexes 2+ symmetric, sensation intact, gait normal. Skin: injection sites clean.
PHQ-9: 2.

Assessment/plan
1. RRMS on interferon beta-1a, clinically quiet. CBC, CMP and TSH today double as her monitoring set.
2. Neurogenic bladder, stable on PRN oxybutynin.
3. Prevention: Pap/HPV co-test done. Flu and bivalent COVID booster given today, left and right arm. Lipids today.

Next visit in about 6 months.

documents.title: Results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Samantha, your Pap came back normal and the HPV test was negative, so the next one isn't due for five years. Blood counts, chemistries, thyroid and cholesterol were all fine as well. I've sent the counts and liver tests to your neurologist.

documents.title: Numb arm and leg
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I wanted to ask about something that's been going on since around September. My left arm and left leg go numb and tingly on and off, sometimes for a few hours. A few times my right eye has gotten blurry and then it clears up by itself after a while. It's not getting worse exactly but it's not going away either and I'm worried it's the MS. Should I see you or neurology?

documents.title: RE: Numb arm and leg
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good morning Samantha. I'm glad you wrote. With your history this needs your neurologist, and they'll likely want a new MRI. I'm messaging the MS clinic this morning to ask for the earliest appointment. If you get sudden vision loss, weakness, or trouble walking or speaking before then, go to the emergency department. Our nurse will call you once we hear back.

documents.title: Call to neurology
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Spoke with MS clinic nurse, shared PCP message. They are giving her a slot on 12/29 and will order an MRI before. Called pt, she has the date. Reviewed ED precautions.

events.reason: intermittent left-sided numbness and right eye blurring

reports.study: MRI brain with and without contrast
reports.text:
MRI BRAIN WITHOUT AND WITH CONTRAST
Indication: multiple sclerosis, intermittent left-sided sensory symptoms and right visual blurring.
Technique: multiplanar multisequence imaging of the brain before and after intravenous gadolinium.
Findings: Multiple ovoid T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions in the periventricular white matter bilaterally. No mass effect. Ventricles and sulci normal in size for age. No acute infarct on diffusion imaging. No hemorrhage. Orbits and visualized sinuses unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Multiple periventricular white matter lesions in this patient with known multiple sclerosis.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY GROUP - MS CLINIC
Date of visit: 12/29/2022

Reason for visit: early return for new symptoms, at the PCP's request.

Ms. Simard is a 30-year-old with relapsing-remitting MS on interferon beta-1a 44 mcg SC three times weekly. Over roughly the last three months she has had recurring spells of numbness and pins-and-needles in the left arm and left leg, and intermittent blurring of vision in the right eye that clears without treatment. No weakness, no gait change.

Medications: interferon beta-1a 44 mcg SC TIW; oxybutynin 5 mg BID as needed.
Allergies: none known.
Social: relocated from the South about two years ago. Does not smoke.

Exam: Afferent pupillary defect on the right. Reflexes brisk in the left arm and left leg compared with the right. Strength full. Remainder of the exam unchanged.

Data:
- 25-OH vitamin D 15 ng/mL (reference 30-100), low.
- CBC, ESR and CRP normal. ANA negative.
- MRI brain with and without contrast (12/27): multiple periventricular white matter lesions.

Impression: RRMS with a mild relapse, left-sided sensory symptoms and right optic nerve involvement; corresponding exam findings. Vitamin D deficiency.

Plan:
1. Continue interferon beta-1a.
2. Start vitamin D3 2000 IU daily.
3. Return as needed for new or worsening symptoms.

Neurology, MS clinic
cc: primary care

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to go over the MS clinic letter from 12/29.

Neurology called it a mild relapse (left-sided sensory spells plus the right eye), staying on interferon. Vitamin D was 15, she started D3 2000 IU right after the visit and takes it with breakfast. Tingling spells still come and go, maybe a little less often. Right eye blurring hasn't happened in a couple of weeks. Bladder same. Feels a bit discouraged that the MS "woke up" after two quiet years, but sleeping and working fine. Declines counseling referral for now.

Exam: vitals as charted. Pupils: subtle right APD, matching the neurology note. Strength full all limbs. Reflexes brisker on the left. Gait normal.

A/P
1. RRMS, recent mild relapse, on interferon beta-1a per neurology. Neurology to see her again as needed.
2. Vitamin D deficiency, on D3 2000 IU. Recheck 25-OH D in about 3 months with her monitoring labs, ordered.
3. Neurogenic bladder, unchanged.
Check in by portal anytime.

events.reason: vitamin D recheck and interferon monitoring

documents.title: Vitamin D
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Samantha, your vitamin D is up to 34, which is in the normal range now. Keep taking the 2000 units every day. The blood counts and liver tests for the interferon were normal too, and I've passed them along to the MS clinic.

documents.title: RE: Vitamin D
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Yay, finally a good number. Thank you!

documents.title: Cancellation
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called, quarter-end at work, can't make tomorrow's follow-up. Doing fine, no new issues. Will just come in for her fall physical. Offered a video slot instead, declined.

documents.title: Oxybutynin refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Electronic refill request, oxybutynin 5 mg #180. Approved by PCP with 1 refill. Physical scheduled 10/17.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
31F, yearly exam.

MS: tingling spells faded out by about March. Has not needed to go back to the MS clinic. Interferon TIW, vitamin D3 daily. Bladder: urgency, no incontinence. Uses oxybutynin most days now rather than a few times a week.

ROS: no vision change, weakness, falls. Mood good.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Eyes: mild right APD, unchanged. Thyroid normal. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Neuro: strength full, reflexes brisker on left, gait normal.
PHQ-9 3.

Plan
- RRMS stable on interferon beta-1a; CBC, CMP and TSH today.
- Vitamin D deficiency, replete on D3.
- Neurogenic bladder: oxybutynin refills sent for the year so she isn't running out.
- Flu and 2023-24 COVID vaccines today. Pap next 2027.
Follow-up in 6 months.

documents.title: Left eye
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Sorry to message on a holiday weekend. Since yesterday my LEFT eye is blurry, like looking through wax paper. Also when I put my chin down I get a zap down my back like an electric shock. My right hand has been tingly on and off for about a month too. I already left a message on the neuro clinic's after-hours line.

documents.title: RE: Left eye
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Samantha, thanks for letting me know. This sounds like it could be another flare and neurology is the right place. Good that you called their line. If they can't see you in the next day or two, or if the vision gets much worse, you lose vision, or you develop weakness, go to the emergency department. Please let me know what they say.

documents.title: RE: Left eye
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Neuro on-call called back. They are fitting me in at their urgent clinic Monday morning and getting an MRI.
